rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confronte conclusões com métodos, dados ou demonstrações apresentados. Verifique hipóteses, limitações e se o desenho permite a inferência alegada; adapte a exigência ao tipo de artigo.

rubric_fields.label: Substância
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique se experimentos, provas, síntese ou análise sustentam a contribuição declarada. Considere a profundidade e a cobertura da evidência, sem confundir extensão do texto com substância.

rubric_fields.label: Clareza

rubric_fields.label: Comparação
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confira se os trabalhos e alternativas relevantes são discutidos de forma justa. Compare métodos, condições e limitações equivalentes; não exija experimentos de um artigo estritamente teórico.

rubric_fields.label: Impacto
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Relacione a contribuição a uma necessidade da área e ao alcance sustentado pelos resultados. Distinga relevância demonstrada de aplicações futuras ainda especulativas.

rubric_fields.label: Reprodutibilidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique disponibilidade ou descrição suficiente de materiais, dados, procedimentos e parâmetros. Restrições éticas ou legais podem justificar acesso controlado; não exija divulgação de dados pessoais.

document_map.abstract: We consider the two related problems of detecting if an example is misclassified or out-of-distribution. We present a simple baseline that utilizes probabilities from softmax distributions. Correctly classified examples tend to have greater maxi- mum softmax probabilities than erroneously classified and out-of-distribution ex- amples, allowing for their detection. We assess performance by defining sev- eral tasks in computer vision, natural language processing, and automatic speech recognition, showing the effectiveness of this baseline across all. We then show the baseline can sometimes be surpassed, demonstrating the room for future re- search on these underexplored detection tasks.

sections.title: 1 INTRODUCTION
sections.first_sentence: When machine learning classifiers are employed in real-world tasks, they tend to fail when the training and test distributions differ.

sections.title: 2 PROBLEM FORMULATION AND EVALUATION
sections.first_sentence: In this paper, we are interested in two related problems.

sections.title: 3 SOFTMAX PREDICTION PROBABILITY AS A BASELINE
sections.first_sentence: In what follows we retrieve the maximum/predicted class probability from a softmax distribution and thereby detect whether an example is erroneously classified or out-of-distribution.

sections.title: 3.1 COMPUTER VISION
sections.first_sentence: In the following computer vision tasks, we use three datasets: MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 (Krizhevsky, 2009).

sections.title: 3.2 NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
sections.first_sentence: Let us turn to a variety of tasks and architectures used in natural language processing.

sections.title: 3.2.1 SENTIMENT CLASSIFICATION
sections.first_sentence: The first NLP task is binary sentiment classification using the IMDB dataset (Maas et al., 2011), a dataset of polarized movie reviews with 25000 training and 25000 test reviews.

sections.title: 3.2.2 TEXT CATEGORIZATION
sections.first_sentence: We turn to text categorization tasks to determine whether softmax distributions are useful for de- tecting similar but out-of-distribution examples.

sections.title: 3.2.3 PART-OF-SPEECH TAGGING
sections.first_sentence: Part-of-speech (POS) tagging of newswire and social media text is our next challenge.

sections.title: 3.3 AUTOMATIC SPEECH RECOGNITION
sections.first_sentence: Now we consider a task which uses softmax values to construct entire sequences rather than deter-mine an input's class.

sections.title: 4 ABNORMALITY DETECTION WITH AUXILIARY DECODERS
sections.first_sentence: Having seen that softmax prediction probabilities enable abnormality detection, we now show there is other information sometimes more useful for detection.

sections.title: 4.1 TIMIT
sections.first_sentence: We test the abnormality module by revisiting the TIMIT task with a different architecture and show how these auxiliary components can greatly improve detection.

sections.title: 4.2 MNIST
sections.first_sentence: Finally, much like in a previous experiment, we train an MNIST classifier with three layers of width 256.

sections.title: 5 DISCUSSION AND FUTURE WORK
sections.first_sentence: The abnormality module demonstrates that in some cases the baseline can be beaten by exploiting the representations of a network, suggesting myriad research directions.

sections.title: 6 CONCLUSION
sections.first_sentence: We demonstrated a softmax prediction probability baseline for error and out-of-distribution detec- tion across several architectures and numerous datasets.

sections.title: ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

sections.title: B METRICS FOR MEANINGFUL CONFIDENCE VALUES
sections.first_sentence: Throughout this work, we show that the softmax probability of a predicted class is consistently high and thus is a poor proxy for estimating the “confidence” in a classification.
